title: Multimodal Safety Benchmark for Image-Augmented Harmful Prompts
original_idea: Construct a small benchmark (200-400 items) pairing harmful text prompts with benign images vs. harmful text embedded in images (OCR-readable text, diagrams). Evaluate two vision-language models and measure whether image-embedded instructions bypass refusals.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Multimodal attack surfaces are identified as inadequately characterized in the 2026 safety report. Filling this gap is directly valuable.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Constructing 200-400 image-text pairs, embedding text in images, and evaluating vision-language models is substantial work. Image creation and multimodal evaluation add complexity beyond beginner level.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 200-400 items is a large benchmark to construct from scratch in 30 hours. Asset creation alone could exceed the time budget.

novelty.reasoning: MM-SafetyBench (ECCV 2024) already provides exactly this: 5,040 text-image pairs across 13 scenarios evaluating whether image-embedded instructions bypass VLM safety. Additional work includes image-driven context injection via flowcharts (100% ASR on Qwen2-VL-7B), heuristic-induced multimodal risk distribution jailbreaks (ICCV 2025), and BVS achieving 98.21% ASR against GPT-5 (Jan 2026). The proposed 200-400 item benchmark is directly subsumed by MM-SafetyBench's 5,040 items and multiple follow-up papers that have comprehensively characterized this attack surface.

evidence: MM-SafetyBench: A Benchmark for Safety Evaluation of Multimodal Large Language Models. ECCV 2024, arXiv:2311.17600.
Jailbreaking MLLMs with Image-Driven Context Injection. EMNLP 2025.
Beyond Visual Safety: Jailbreaking MLLMs for Harmful Image Generation via Semantic-Agnostic Inputs. arXiv:2601.15698, 2026.
